issue_context.title: Regression introduced by new min max validators
issue_context.body:
# Bug Report ### Affected Package @angular/forms 12+ ### Is this a regression? Yes, the previous version in which this bug was not present was: 11 ### Description @angular/forms 12 introduced min and max validators based on the min and max attributes presence in #39063. Before that, the browser would react to min/max attributes by doing validation and also by preventing to introduce invalid value. Both of those **native features are now impossible to leverage**. Also, before that, it was possible to deactivate the browser native features with a null value, such as `[min]="null"` or `[min]="undefined"`. This is now impossible to do in strict mode compilation, because the new directive only accept `string | number` and would **result in a compilation error**. Possible temporary workaround for that is to use `$any` casting similar to `[min]="configuration.min ?? $any(undefined)"` ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/72603/119329150-def05580-bcbf-11eb-8131-d490496b6b82.png) ### Suggested fixes I would suggest that both directives create, and maintain, the equivalent attribute on the HTMLInputElement, so that browsers are able to react accordingly and adapt their UX. And I would suggest to loosen the input type like so: ```diff - @Input() min!: string|number; + @Input() min: string|number|null|undefined; ``` If those suggestions sound mergeable I could create PRs for it. ## Minimal Reproduction - https://stackblitz.com/edit/min-max-regression-angular-11 - https://stackblitz.com/edit/min-max-regression-angular-12, same as above, but with strict mode disabled, and Angular 12 ## Exception or Error ``` Type 'number | null' is not assignable to type 'string | number'. ``` ## Your Environment **Angular Version:** 

Angular CLI: 12.0.1
Node: 14.17.0
Package Manager: yarn 1.22.5
OS: linux x64

comments: @sonukapoor, since you wrote the PR that brought this regression, would you have any particular opinions about this issue ? were those use-cases considered in your PR ?

> > @sonukapoor, since you wrote the PR that brought this regression, would you have any particular opinions about this issue ? were those use-cases considered in your PR ?
> 
> @PowerKiKi I do not think this use case of null/undefined was considered.
> @iRealNirmal let us know if you need any help with that.

Sure @sonukapoor

Hi, thanks for reporting the issue. 

Just want to provide a bit more context after initial investigation. The `min`/`max` validators were modeled after `minlength`/`maxlength` ones, which have the input type defined as `string|number`:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/4ac55ca676769a54a76c5881d40109b556f497b7/packages/forms/src/directives/validators.ts#L553-L554

However in the code below the input value is checked against `null` and `undefined` values as well:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/4ac55ca676769a54a76c5881d40109b556f497b7/packages/forms/src/directives/validators.ts#L569-L571

So the `minlength` and `maxlength` directives would have the same problem from types perspective, but would work as expected (no validation happening) if the value is `null` or `undefined`.

It looks like the `min` and `max` validators work with `null` and `undefined` by accident where these values are [converted to `NaN`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/forms/src/directives/validators.ts#L241) and after that the comparison with a number always gives `false`, so the underlying [minValidator](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/bf505ad7071f54f44b4bfc18155e55599002e668/packages/forms/src/validators.ts#L424) and [maxValidator](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/bf505ad7071f54f44b4bfc18155e55599002e668/packages/forms/src/validators.ts#L440) functions return "validation is successful" result.

Looking at other validator directives in the [packages/forms/src/directives/validators.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/forms/src/directives/validators.ts) file, some of them have special checks for when validator should be enabled, such as the [required](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/forms/src/directives/validators.ts#L357) validator, but in some cases (for example in [the pattern validator](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/forms/src/directives/validators.ts#L727)), the validation will always happen and there is no way to conditionally enable/disable it.

My conclusion is that we should revisit all existing form validators (not only `min` and `max`) from that perspective and make sure that the logic is consistent. Specifically verify (by adding tests) that there is a way to conditionally disable validation, update input types accordingly (to allow for `null|undefined` types) and mention this behavior in docs.
I would think you can workaround this issue by binding to `[attr.min]` instead, fwiw.

> `min` and `max` validators work with `null` and `undefined` by accident

Exactly my conclusion too. I read the code first and expected it to fail, but was surprised when I tried and it actually worked. That's definitely something that will need to be supported explicitly, and not accidentally.

> I would think you can workaround this issue by binding to `[attr.min]` instead, fwiw.

Excellent suggestion ! I wish I thought about that yesterday. This allows to keep using the browsers native features (:+1:). And it also avoid having a duplicated validators (:+1:): the one I already explicitly added by code before Angular 12, and the one auto-magically injected since Angular 12. Thanks @Airblader !

I would go as far as saying that this is not just a workaround, but it actually **is the proper permanent solution** for people who manage their validator by code (as opposed to templates). And it should probably have been mentioned in the migration notes.

And I'll go a bit off-topic, but this reminds me of the situation of the `required` validator, https://github.com/angular/components/issues/2574, where the validator should impact the template (to show the `*`), and not the other way round. Here too, for people working with reactive forms, the validator defined by code should drive the template.

As far as I am concerned, I am no longer impacted by this issue, but I still think it should be fixed.

@iRealNirmal I re-created the reproduction as https://github.com/PowerKiKi/angular-issue-42267#readme. I made [only one simple commit](https://github.com/PowerKiKi/angular-issue-42267/commit/6d426d2a944e86bdf64770c3a99525fbc9718af2) after the app generation with angular-cli. So you should be able to clone and reproduce locally with that and see that it does not compile, but I expect to compile fine.

> As discussed offline the min attribute is being removed when the value is 0 is because of this host binding:

Great catch @iRealNirmal and @petebacondarwin 👍 

The same problem can technically affect `minlength` and `maxlength` validators:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/c110d050f247f569b2e95bd7787ef2dfeff8beac/packages/forms/src/directives/validators.ts#L540-L544

But semantically it just doesn't make sense to set `minlength` and `maxlength` to `0`, so that's why we haven't seen this issue there, but having `0` as an input to the `min` and `max` validators makes sense.
This issue is **not** solved until #42378 is also merged. But I cannot re-open the issue myself.
